newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Brent to test lower, first support $18.08.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Brent to test lower, first support $18.08.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures are expected to test lower on Wednesday but support is expected to be encountered at $18.08, the low point of Tuesday's move, traders said.
August Brent closed 19 cents a barrel up on Tuesday at $18.38 a barrel while July gas oil, which expires on Thursday, was $1.50 up at $162.75 a tonne.
Charles Gray at Prudential Bache futures in London said he saw Brent trading lower on SIMEX and a move downwards would encounter support at $18.08, the low point of Tuesday's price action.

But he said the impact of recent fundamental news on the market may be relatively short-lived, and if the market rallied again, the first important resistance point to be found would appear at $19.24, the mid-point of Tuesday's range.
This level also lies just beneath the high points of Friday's and Monday's price action at $18.27 and $18.28.
Tom James at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore saw support at $18.11 and $17.97 a barrel. The latter number is the recent low formed on Monday.
He pegged trendline resistance up at $18.38 and then $18.51.

Gas oil, he said, would find resistance at previous congestion areas at $161.00 and $162.25, while resistance would be found at $164.00 and $164.25 - levels corresponding to a gap on the continuation chart from last Thursday to Friday.
